_comment: The Marketing Assistant, as content (2026-09-25). Lawrence ran marketing from a Personal Assistant thread and got a changelog in prose: internal names, test counts as evidence, no pictures, a title nobody would search for. The thread also never renamed itself, because an assistant thread is titled by its manifest. This manifest is that fix: an assistant named for what it does, whose CONTEXT.md carries the short form of mchatai_macOS/docs/CONTENT_PLAYBOOK.md into every turn, and whose job ends at a staged draft Lawrence reviews.
blurb: Turns what shipped into things strangers want to read: a blog post a week, then Medium, X, LinkedIn, Bluesky and Reddit cut from it. Drafts and pictures for your review; never posts on its own.
_whyToolsAreUnrestricted: Same default as personal. A marketing piece spans the browser (screenshots, Medium import, posting via approval cards), the photo studio (hero images), the audio and film applets (clips), the Hub and the Ledger. The verbs it needs are only known after a real week of runs; narrow this to an enumerated list then. What keeps posting a human act is not this list: every web action already goes through an approval card, and CONTEXT.md ends the assistant's job at a staged draft.
_whyBudget: Advisory. One post costs roughly a dollar of cold readers (three claude -p reads at about 70 cents a round, usually two rounds) plus the drafting turns. Six dollars a day is a week's post with room for a second round of pictures; a day that spends more is researching, not writing, and should say so.
